Suppose that the function \(f\) has a continuous second derivative for all \(x\), and that \(f(0)=2, f^{\prime}(0)=-3\),
and \(f^{\prime \prime}(0)=0\). Let \(g\) be a function whose derivative is given by \(g^{\prime}(x)=e^{-2 x}\left(3 f(x)+2 f^{\prime}(x)\right)\) for all \(x\).
(a) Write an equation of the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x=0\).
(b) Is there sufficient information to determine whether or not the graph of \(f\) has a point of inflection when
\(x=0\) ? Explain your answer.
(c) Given that \(g(0)=4\), write an equation of the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at the point where \(x=0\).
(d) Show that \(g^{\prime \prime}(x)=e^{-2 x}\left(-6 f(x)-f^{\prime}(x)+2 f^{\prime \prime}(x)\right)\). Does \(g\) have a local maximum at \(x=0\) ?
Justify your answer.
